patch: Liraasa 3.3 — Archetypes and the top 2,000 (supersedes the separate 3.2 draft)
status: PROPOSED: ratify tier 1 first; tier 2 may be ratified, deferred or dropped item by item
principles: Compaction: a few short roots carry many meanings through archetype compounds (3.2:G142).
Short CVCV roots, the scarcest spellings, are spent only on high-frequency archetype words.
Where a concept is already sayable, it is documented as a recipe instead of a word.
Tier 1 = high-frequency fiction gaps; tier 2 = optional.

function_words_add.use: Standalone reply or clause-initial with a comma; everyday register only. zabo stays the plain 'yes'.

rulings_add.rule: A small set of archetype modifiers combines with archetype heads to name kinds of a thing. Modifiers: gudo (common, ordinary), zile (fine, fancy), farvi (wild), yalmu (powered), krono (aged), and any time or place noun. Heads: pocu (fowl), kadu (vehicle), kaze (gun), velma (clothing), nami (food), miru (infused drink), favro (signal device), bujo (joint), nela (person). A pair is read 'the MODIFIER sort of HEAD', but its listed meaning is binding and specific: gudopocu is chicken, not any common bird. Unlisted pairs may be coined by rule and must be flagged until listed. -vu (big) and -ti (small) apply as usual: pocuvu turkey, pocuti chick.
In eating and cooking, an animal noun also names its meat, as English chicken and fish do: sapusia gudopocu, to eat chicken. yugenami (meat) remains the general word; X de yugenami is never needed.

Body-part nouns double as units of length when they follow a number: pebu (a foot), fini (a finger-width, roughly an inch), varo (an arm-length, roughly a yard). valmilornu (an hour's walk) is the long unit. cono (coin) is the generic money unit.

zilenela placed directly before a name, with no comma, is an honorific title: Mr, Mrs, Ms. As a vocative, iya zilenela is sir or madam. A kinship or rank word may stand before a name the same way (pilo Peta, Father Peta).

Further archetype heads under 3.2:G142: furo (fruit; a colour base names the fruit: rubifuro apple, aurumifuro lemon, viofuroti grape), herba (plant, vegetable), marna (grain), pusa (powder), nami (dish), kova (container), biti (tool), velma (garment), rinba (ring, jewelry), zupa (room), domlu (building). Listed meanings are binding; unlisted pairs are flagged.
A copied place name (2.0:G45) + -san is an adjective of origin: Fransa + -san = Fransasan, French. The bare name stays a noun; de + the name means from the place.

rulings_add.topic: Relational adjectives from compounds and derivations
rulings_add.rule: The adjective slot (-san) of any compound, listed derivation or image compound is available by rule, with the reading 'of, relating to, or marked by X', unless the lexicon lists another meaning for it. For roots, only listed forms exist (unchanged). This supplies English relational adjectives (theological, railway, comic, muddy, distant) without listing each one.
